data.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** e7855920a7b5ce38d2043d435568ee439dd8aa56
* **Plugin:** dso-dev v1.16.11
* **Affected:** entire `plugins/dso/agents/` tree (41 .md files) + plugin manifest
* **Active session:** all named-agent dispatches throughout this session (review, investigation, classification) used general-purpose fallback

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

The DSO plugin ships 41 agent definitions at `plugins/dso/agents/\*.md`, each with proper frontmatter (`name:`, `model:`, `description:`). REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md Step 4 explicitly documents:

> "Use the registered subagent_type directly — `dso:code-reviewer-*` are valid Agent tool subagent_type values in this environment. Do NOT substitute `subagent_type: 'general-purpose'` with a constructed prompt."

The expected behavior is that all 41 `dso:<name>` identifiers appear as registered subagent_type values in the Agent tool's available list, so dispatchers can use them directly with native runtime support (per-agent permissions, model selection, telemetry). The plugin's installation should register agent files with the Claude Code runtime such that they are visible to the Agent tool.

#### Actual Behavior

**0 of 41 dso agents are registered as subagent_type values in this session.**

The Claude Code runtime's available subagent_type list (from system prompt at session start):
- claude-code-guide
- Explore
- general-purpose
- Plan
- statusline-setup

None of the 41 `dso:*` agents appear:

```
$ ls plugins/dso/agents/*.md | xargs -I{} basename {} .md | sort
approach-decision-maker
bloat-blue-team
bloat-resolver
blue-team-filter
bot-psychologist
code-reviewer-deep-arch
code-reviewer-deep-correctness
code-reviewer-deep-hygiene
code-reviewer-deep-verification
code-reviewer-light
code-reviewer-performance
code-reviewer-security-blue-team
code-reviewer-security-red-team
code-reviewer-standard
code-reviewer-test-quality
completion-verifier
complexity-evaluator
conflict-analyzer
cross-epic-interaction-classifier
doc-writer
feasibility-reviewer
huge-diff-refactor-anomaly
huge-diff-reviewer-light
huge-diff-reviewer-standard
inference-incident-curator
intent-search
investigator-advanced-code-tracer
investigator-advanced-historical
investigator-basic
investigator-escalated-code-tracer
investigator-escalated-empirical
investigator-escalated-history
investigator-escalated-web
investigator-intermediate
investigator-intermediate-fallback
plan-review
red-team-reviewer
red-test-evaluator
red-test-writer
scope-drift-reviewer
ui-designer
```

Net effect: every named-agent dispatch in DSO workflows falls back to `subagent_type: "general-purpose"` with the agent body inlined verbatim. This session alone made ~10 such dispatches (review pass 1/2/3 standard + security + test-quality + performance overlay + investigator-intermediate + complexity assessments). Each pays the cost of inlining ~600 lines of agent body in the prompt and forfeits per-agent telemetry/permissions.

**Documentation contradiction adds confusion:**

CLAUDE.md and multiple SKILL.md files explicitly state the `dso:*` names are NOT valid subagent_type values:

```
plugins/dso/skills/sprint/SKILL.md:
  "(`dso:complexity-evaluator` is an agent file identifier, NOT a valid `subagent_type` — the Agent tool only accepts built-in types.)"

plugins/dso/skills/resolve-conflicts/SKILL.md (similar):
  "(`dso:conflict-analyzer` is an agent file identifier, NOT a valid `subagent_type` value — the Agent tool only accepts built-in types.)"
```

This contradicts REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md Step 4 which says they ARE valid. CLAUDE.md "Architecture" section attempts to reconcile by saying:

> "Use `subagent_type: 'dso:<name>'` directly when the agent is registered in the Agent tool's available types list. Fall back to `subagent_type: 'general-purpose'` with the agent file loaded verbatim only when the named type is not registered."

But in practice, the named types are NEVER registered (verified in this session and consistent with the contradictory text elsewhere). The "fall back" branch is the only path that ever executes.

### 3. Action History and Workarounds

* **Steps Taken (this session, evidence):**
  * Dispatched standard tier reviewer 3 times across PR #62 fix passes — each used `subagent_type: "general-purpose"` with `code-reviewer-standard.md` body inlined (~663 lines)
  * Dispatched test-quality, security-red-team, performance overlays in pass 1 — same pattern
  * Dispatched investigator-intermediate (opus) for cb67-2265 root-cause analysis — same pattern
  * Dispatched red-test-writer for the f2c7-257e RED test — same pattern
* **Raw Results:**
  * Each prompt inflated by 600+ lines of inlined agent body
  * No per-agent telemetry exists for any of these dispatches
  * The session's available subagent_type list never grew beyond the 5 built-ins
* **Known Workarounds:** Continue using the documented fallback path. Functional but inefficient and breaks the named-agent's permission boundaries.

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* All 41 files in `plugins/dso/agents/`
* `plugins/dso/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and `plugin.json` (plugin manifest — likely missing the agent registration mechanism)
* CLAUDE.md "Architecture / Named-agent dispatch" section
* REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md Step 4 (states agents ARE registered — contradicts reality)
* Multiple SKILL.md files (state agents are NOT valid subagent_types — matches reality)
* Existing related ticket: `be13-a9e9-a44f-467b` (code-reviewer-* subset of this issue, filed earlier this session)

### 6. Logs

```
$ ls plugins/dso/agents/*.md | wc -l
41

# Available subagent types this session (from system prompt):
#   claude-code-guide, Explore, general-purpose, Plan, statusline-setup
# (no dso:* entries)

$ grep -c "dso:" plugins/dso/skills/**/SKILL.md
# many matches — references the agents by name, but every one falls back to general-purpose
```

#### Suggested fix scope

This is a plugin distribution / registration bug. Two-part fix:

**Part 1 — Resolve the documentation contradiction (immediate):**

Either:
(a) The agents SHOULD be registered. Update CLAUDE.md "Architecture" section and the per-skill "agent file identifier, NOT a valid subagent_type" comments to remove the contradicting text. Then make Part 2 an actual hard requirement.

OR

(b) The agents are intentionally not registered and "agent file + verbatim body" is the official pattern. Update REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md Step 4 to remove the "Use the registered subagent_type directly" claim. Document the verbatim-inlining as the canonical path everywhere consistently.

Until this is decided, half the dispatchers expect (a), half assume (b), and the runtime always behaves as (b).

**Part 2 — If (a) is the chosen direction, implement registration:**

Investigate Claude Code's plugin manifest schema (`plugin.json` and/or `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) for an `agents` field or registration mechanism. Add explicit entries pointing the runtime at each `plugins/dso/agents/<name>.md` file with frontmatter parsing. Verify that after `/plugin sync` (or equivalent) the 41 agents appear in the session's subagent_type list.

Add a smoke test to the plugin install flow asserting that `dso:complexity-evaluator` (or another representative agent) is registered post-install.

This is bug priority 2 (medium) — every DSO workflow operates correctly through the fallback, but the contradiction creates friction every time an agent reads the docs and the inlining pattern wastes prompt tokens on a per-dispatch basis.
data.title: [plugin agent registration]: 41 dso:* agent files exist -> 0 registered as Agent tool subagent_type values; CLAUDE.md vs REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md contradict each other on whether registration is expected
